children: , the semiconductor-equipment and materials-engineering company, fell about 1.6% to $533.59 around 11:39 a.m. ET Tuesday, despite a bullish Goldman Sachs outlook. According to Barron's, Goldman rates the shares Buy and expects stronger margin targets and growth guidance. But after the stock more than doubled this year, another upbeat forecast faces a high bar.

Applied reported record fiscal third-quarter revenue of $9.12 billion, up 25% from a year earlier, with a GAAP gross margin of 50.3%. Management pointed to demand from leading-edge logic, DRAM and advanced packaging while outlining manufacturing-capacity investments through the decade. The business is growing fast. The next question is how much of that growth reaches the bottom line as expansion spending rises.

The valuation graphic puts the shares 110.86% above the $253.05 GF Value estimate, suggesting little room for disappointment against that benchmark. That estimate is no guaranteed destination, but the gap sharpens the investment test. Applied needs to turn stronger chip demand into durable profitability while absorbing capacity, staffing and development costs. More AI spending supports the revenue story. Better margins would give investors a stronger reason to pay up.

title: Applied Materials Stock Falls 1.6% as Goldman Bets Margins Still Have Room
